description:
The adopter-facing command reference describes how a profile command is told where its package is, so the flag the resolver added is documented where adopters read command syntax.

## Background

The profile commands and the profiled initialization gained a way to name the repository location a package is read from. Until that is written down, an adopter meets it only in `--help`, and the reference that documents every other flag of those commands is silently incomplete.

What it says is the resolution order, because that is what an adopter needs to predict: a supplied location wins, the location the repository's own record names is used when none is supplied, and a recorded location that no longer resolves is an error rather than an absent profile.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The command reference describes the supplied-location form on every command that accepts it, including profiled initialization.
- [hard] REQ-02: It states the resolution order and what happens when a recorded location no longer resolves.
- [hard] REQ-03: The fact has one home: other pages needing it cite the reference rather than restating it.
- [hard] REQ-04: The mechanical documentation checks pass over the changed pages.

## Notes

What a package is and where an adopter obtains one belongs to the profile reference, not here; this page covers command syntax.
title: Describe the supplied-location form in the command reference
